functionalObligations.text: USDG is an electronic-money claim with two obligors selected by the holder's residence: for EEA holders the issuer is Paxos Issuance Europe Oy, a Finnish electronic money institution supervised by the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority under LEI 743700KYSSTKZYGEUF50 and Business ID 3236886-2; for everyone else the issuer is Paxos Digital Singapore Pte. Ltd., a Major Payments Institution supervised by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a CORPUS CORRECTION. The corpus says USDG's distinguishing legal fact is 'the NYDFS trust charter'. USDG is not issued under a NYDFS trust charter at all; it is issued by a Singapore MPI and a Finnish EMI under MiCA. The residue item is right that a charter distinction exists and wrong about which charter. Beyond that: no symbol can express an obligor that varies by who is asking. The same structure appears at USDC (US LLC / French SAS), so two of the five are two instruments under one ticker.

functionalObligations.text: Holders have a right of redemption at any time and at par value, stated in the regulator's prescribed language -- 1 USDG = 1 USD, without incurring fees, on a one-for-one basis notwithstanding any change in the market value of stablecoins or reserve assets -- with tokens burned on redemption.
functionalObligations.note: The STRONGEST Rd of the five and the only one that is a regulatory entitlement rather than a contractual facility: at any time, at par, no fee, no minimum, and unconditional on the market value of the reserve. It remains APPROXIMATE for the same structural reason as the other four -- all redemptions are subject to compliance review and may be delayed, and no on-chain path exists -- but the difference between this and USDT's 819 customers at a US$100,000 minimum with a greater-of-US$1,000-or-0.1% fee is the widest spread in the category, and Rd is the same symbol at both ends of it.

functionalObligations.text: Minting is available exclusively on the Paxos Platform to institutions that have successfully completed the requisite onboarding procedures, so issuance and redemption are asymmetric: anyone may redeem, only onboarded institutions may mint.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE -- an off-chain onboarding gate, coded on the corpus's own USDC reasoning. CORPUS DEPARTURE: Aw is ADDED. Note the asymmetry itself is residue: no element can express that entry to a system is gated while exit is not, which is the opposite of the USDT and USD1 pattern where exit is gated and entry to the secondary market is not.

functionalObligations.text: Issuance destinations are whitelisted on-chain: the SupplyControl contract at 0x9a7164112029b81c07636ab7b59fa813e0883bbf exposes addMintAddressToWhitelist, removeMintAddressFromWhitelist, updateAllowAnyMintAndBurnAddress and the predicates canMintToAddress and canBurnFromAddress, so where new supply may be sent is enforced by contract rather than by policy.
functionalObligations.note: FIRM -- the only genuinely ON-CHAIN Aw in the category. Every other permission gate among the five is a business relationship; this one is a predicate the contract evaluates. It is issuer-side rather than user-side (holders face no gate) which is the same qualification the bridges lane attached to Aw for WBTC's merchant registry.

functionalObligations.text: Each supply controller's minting is rate-limited on-chain: SupplyControl carries per-controller limit configuration through contracts/lib/RateLimit.sol, with updateLimitConfig and getRemainingMintAmount, under SUPPLY_CONTROLLER_MANAGER_ROLE, SUPPLY_CONTROLLER_ROLE and TOKEN_CONTRACT_ROLE.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the run's THIRD independent arrival at one schema. The yield lane and the CDP lane both found a five-part primitive -- named agent, domain whitelist, magnitude cap, rate-of-change limit or delay, revocation -- bounding an allocation and a rate respectively. SupplyControl instantiates the identical schema bounding ISSUANCE: a named supply controller, a mint-address whitelist (F4), a per-period cap, a remaining-amount limiter, and role revocation. Three lanes, three categories, three different bounded quantities, one shape. It is also the mitigation an X9-style single-key-mint concern would demand, and the vocabulary cannot record that the mitigation exists. Ct was considered and rejected: Ct is a collateral or margin test on a position, not a rate limit on an authority.

functionalObligations.text: The reserve is at least 100% of outstanding EU-attributed USDG in high-quality, low-risk assets such as cash and short-term government debt, legally segregated from the issuer's own funds and from the custodian's funds, held with qualified custodians, authorised by the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority and structured for bankruptcy remoteness, with MiCA additionally requiring a portion to sit with European banking partners.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Named custodians and named banking partners: UNKNOWN from primary sources. Note what is different here and equally unnameable: the reserve is not merely disclosed, it is CONSTRAINED BY A REGULATOR and held in trust accounts the regulator authorised. A supervised, segregated, bankruptcy-remote reserve and Tether's discretionary portfolio of gold, bitcoin and secured loans are the same symbol.

functionalObligations.text: In insolvency holders are entitled to a proportionate share of the segregated reserve assets, with their claims taking precedence over unsecured creditors, distributed under Finnish insolvency law and overseen by the insolvency administrator and the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. This is the strongest creditor position of the five and it decomposes identically to the weakest. Tr (tranche waterfall) was considered and REJECTED for the same reason as at USDT F2, but note how close it comes: law L6's terms for Tr are declared seniority (yes -- priority over unsecured creditors), dispute forum (yes -- the District Court of Helsinki, F9), and a recovery-timing assumption (partly -- Finnish insolvency procedure). Three of L6's terms are satisfied entirely off-chain. Tr is withheld because no mechanism executes the waterfall. Stage 4 should note that a law whose terms are satisfiable outside the algebra cannot discriminate constructions inside it.

functionalObligations.text: USDG is not covered by any investor compensation or deposit guarantee scheme: white paper field D.11 is false for both Directive 97/9/EC and Directive 2014/49/EU, though the underlying segregated accounts are.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. The distinction between an instrument covered by a guarantee scheme and one whose reserve accounts are covered while the instrument is not is a two-level protection structure with no representation, and it is the same trap as USD1's FDIC-limit caveat: the retail mental model of 'it is in a bank' is exactly what these two disclosures deny.

functionalObligations.text: The governing law is the law of Finland and the competent court is the District Court of Helsinki.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. There is no symbol for a FORUM. 'Who do you sue, and where' is answerable from primary documents for three of the five -- a Helsinki court here, confidential BVI-law arbitration seated in London for USDT, US courts under the BitGo terms for USD1 -- and unrepresentable for all five. Law L6 lists a dispute forum among Tr's terms, so the carrier's own constraint language references an object its element set cannot name.

functionalObligations.text: Assurance is monthly under Singapore standards: reports posted on or after 2026-02-27 are issued by KPMG LLP under standards established by the Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants, and earlier reports by Enrome LLP under the same standards, indexed monthly for 2024, 2025 and January to June 2026.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://www.paxos.com/usdg-transparency (accessed 2026-08-04, content read via a rendered browser fetch) | https://globaldollar.com/about-usdg (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and the most degraded At of the five in practice. USDG is the only member attested under a non-US, non-ISAE standard -- ISCA rather than AICPA or ISAE 3000R -- which the corpus does not record and which matters for what At means. Worse: the per-month report PDFs are served through a JavaScript viewer that stage 1 could not resolve to direct URLs even under a rendered browser fetch, so THE ATTESTED RESERVE FIGURES AND COMPOSITION FOR USDG ARE UNKNOWN IN THIS RECORD. At marks the presence of an attestation and cannot record that the attestation is not retrievable. That is L27's staleness-and-recourse gap in its most acute form: an attestation nobody can read is indistinguishable, in the model, from one everybody can.

functionalObligations.text: Reserve revenue is passed back to Global Dollar Network partners rather than kept by the issuer, and the distribution is implemented on-chain: the deployed implementation contains ClaimableRewardsBase and ClaimableRewardsStorageV3 with payout groups, per-wallet shares, period accounting, _claimIndividualRewardsWithData and an individual claim path, audited by Zellic as 'USDG Rewards'.
functionalObligations.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE, and the most consequential correction in this category. The corpus marks Fd as FORCED with the reason 'the surplus distribution is a legal agreement executed by wire, not an on-chain fee flow', and uses that as evidence for the category's central thesis. The premise is factually wrong: the deployed, verified implementation carries a rewards ledger with accrual, share accounting and a claim function, and it has been independently audited under that name. Fd IS NOT A FORCED FIT. Sh is APPROXIMATE -- shares are pro-rata within a payout group, but the pool they claim against is a stream of off-chain-funded reward rather than a pool of held assets. Ep is APPROXIMATE -- accrual is period-based (getCurrentPeriodNum, calculatePeriodsCrossed) which is an epoch-gated transition on the reward, not on the token. Ix was considered and REJECTED: no single global index was evidenced; the accounting is per-payout-group with a projected multiplier (projectMultiplier, MultiplierGrowthLib), which is index-LIKE and not shown to be an index.

functionalObligations.text: Reward entitlement survives a transfer of the token: updateSharesWithRewardPreservation, _transferWithDifferentPayouts and _updateWalletWithPayoutGroup re-attribute reward shares between payout groups when balances move.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. This is a real accounting mechanism attached to an ERC-20 transfer and it is neither Rb (nominal balances do not change) nor plain Sh (the share moves between claimants, not the claim between holders). A transfer simultaneously moves a balance and re-prices two third parties' entitlements. Nothing in the claims-and-accounting group can state that.

functionalObligations.text: The money funding the on-chain rewards ledger is off-chain reserve income paid under partner agreements on three distinct bases -- average USDG balance held, net USDG minted, and USDG transaction volume -- with an explicit disclaimer that nothing displayed constitutes a commitment or obligation to pay any particular amount.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the precise boundary of F11. The DISTRIBUTION is on-chain; the SOURCE and the OBLIGATION are not, and the issuer states in terms that there is no obligation. So the construction can name the payout rail and cannot name whether anything is paid into it. The specific revenue-share percentage is UNKNOWN from primary sources; figures of '97%' and 'over 90%' circulate in secondary coverage and were not confirmed at the issuer, and are not carried.

functionalObligations.text: An asset-protection authority may freeze an address and wipe a frozen balance: the enforcement predicates _isAddrFrozen and whenNotPaused sit in the token's own transfer path in contracts/lib/PaxosBaseAbstract.sol under ASSET_PROTECTION_ROLE.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xfacd5ff359adf87822374275699dd518aaf9a65f (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call getFacet(0x8d1fdf2f) and getFacet(0xe2f72f03) at 0xe343167631d89b6FFc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D, both returning 0xe90c0e2fecd06c5875b50f6b13f3b8dbdb4ce946 (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE REGISTER, used with a note, and carried on a verification stage 1 did not perform. freeze(address) and wipeFrozenAddress(address) are NOT in the implementation's ABI: they are reached through the facet router and currently route to the admin facet at 0xe90c0e2f..., confirmed by reading the live facet table on 2026-08-04. The enforcement lives in the token; the entry points live in a mutable dispatch table. See F18.

functionalObligations.text: A pause authority may halt transfers: PAUSE_ROLE gates pause() and unpause(), which route through the facet table to 0xe90c0e2fecd06c5875b50f6b13f3b8dbdb4ce946, and the whenNotPaused modifier is enforced in the token's transfer path.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call getFacet(0x8456cb59) and getFacet(0x3f4ba83a) at 0xe343167631d89b6FFc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D, both returning 0xe90c0e2fecd06c5875b50f6b13f3b8dbdb4ce946 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xfacd5ff359adf87822374275699dd518aaf9a65f (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: Gp is ADDED, and this is the member where the correction needed real work. A naive ABI read of USDG's implementation shows NO pause function, which would wrongly suggest USDG lacks Gp; the capability exists because the facet table maps the pause selectors. Verified by direct eth_call on the live table on 2026-08-04. With this, Gp is established as present and live in all five deployed tokens -- the corpus coded it in one.

functionalObligations.text: A holder may authorise transfers by signature: permit, transferWithAuthorization and cancelAuthorization route through the facet table to an authorisation facet at 0x7569ae2be6ac51ed7f92f8167090b52615f86497, and the implementation reserves the EIP-712, EIP-2612 and EIP-3009 storage slots in contracts/BaseStorageV3.sol.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call getFacet(0xd505accf), getFacet(0xe3ee160e), getFacet(0x5a049a70) at 0xe343167631d89b6FFc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D, all returning 0x7569ae2be6ac51ed7f92f8167090b52615f86497 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xfacd5ff359adf87822374275699dd518aaf9a65f (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and a NEW ASSIGNMENT the corpus codes for none of the five. Law L17's four terms are satisfied exactly by an EIP-3009 authorisation (bounded scope, cancelAuthorization, validAfter/validBefore, nonce under an EIP-712 domain). Approximate only against Au's 'session policy' gloss. As with F14 and F15 the capability is facet-routed and was established by reading the live table, not by inheriting a claim.

functionalObligations.text: The implementation is reached through an EIP-1967 proxy at 0xe343167631d89b6FFc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D and upgrades under UUPS -- upgradeTo, upgradeToAndCall and proxiableUUID live in the implementation USDG at 0xfaCd5Ff359aDF87822374275699DD518aaf9A65f, solc 0.8.28, fully verified 2026-02-27.
functionalObligations.note: Firm fit, and the only member of the five whose upgrade logic lives in the implementation rather than the proxy -- a different failure mode (an implementation without upgradeTo bricks the proxy) that Up cannot distinguish from a transparent proxy, an EIP-1967 proxy, or USDT's five-function forwarding deprecation. Source is MIT at github.com/paxosglobal/usdg-contract and github.com/paxosglobal/paxos-token-contracts; byte-for-byte repo-to-deployment comparison was NOT performed and is not asserted. Note that the deployed verified sources include hardhat/console.sol among the compiled units.

functionalObligations.text: Beneath the proxy the token carries a second, finer mutability surface: a facet router with setFacet(bytes4,address) and batchSetFacet(FacetCut[]) under DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, a facets mapping, and a fallback() that delegatecalls facets[msg.sig] and reverts with FacetNotFound when the selector is unmapped.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xfacd5ff359adf87822374275699dd518aaf9a65f (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call getFacet(bytes4) at 0xe343167631d89b6FFc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D across the pause, freeze, wipe, permit and EIP-3009 selectors (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the sharpest new finding in this record. Up is one bit; USDG has THREE NESTED MUTABILITY SURFACES -- proxy, implementation, per-selector facet table -- and the consequence is not merely that upgrades are finer-grained. It is that FOUR OF USDG'S OWN ELEMENTS EXIST ONLY BECAUSE A MUTABLE TABLE MAPS THEIR SELECTORS: Gp (F15), Fz (F14), Au (F16) and part of Fd (F11) are all facet-routed, and a single setFacet(selector, address(0)) removes any of them, after which the call reverts FacetNotFound. So an element set for USDG is a statement about the contents of an admin-controlled dispatch table at a block height, not about the code. The vocabulary has no way to say 'present, and revocable by table edit', and this is the third and strongest instance of the category-level gap first seen at USDT's dormant fee dial and USD1's null-but-installable checker: THE VOCABULARY DESCRIBES WHAT IS, NOT WHAT IS ARMED OR WHAT IS REVOCABLE.

functionalObligations.text: Every one of those mutability surfaces sits behind a 24-hour delay: owner() and defaultAdmin() are both 0x9036566EAa5f83e0b9E1161C6C602B0aDF997654, a verified TimelockController whose getMinDelay() returns 86400, and hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, that timelock) returns true, so setFacet, batchSetFacet and the UUPS upgrade are all delayed.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call defaultAdmin() at 0xe343167631d89b6FFc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D returning 0x9036566eaa5f83e0b9e1161c6c602b0adf997654, getMinDelay() at that address returning 0x15180 (86400), and hasRole(0x00..00, 0x9036566e...) returning 1 (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: Tg is ADDED, and it is the single sharpest GOVERNANCE difference in the category -- present in exactly one of the five and coded in none. USDG is the ONLY member that satisfies law L15 (Up -> Tg | bounded emergency process). USDT is a 3-of-6 multisig with no delay, USDC's proxy admin is a bare EOA, USD1's is a 3-of-5 Safe with no delay, PYUSD's is a bare EOA. The corpus lists armedProhibitions: [] for all five, which is the same answer for the one system that has a delay and the four that do not. This obligation is why the corpus's control-plane coding cannot be trusted as a discriminator: it recorded no difference where the only real one lives.

functionalObligations.text: A separate and much shorter delay governs handover of the admin role itself: defaultAdminDelay() returns 10800, three hours, on transferring DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, alongside beginDefaultAdminTransfer, acceptDefaultAdminTransfer, cancelDefaultAdminTransfer, changeDefaultAdminDelay and rollbackDefaultAdminDelay.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Two delays of different lengths govern different things -- 86400 seconds on what the admin DOES, 10800 seconds on WHO THE ADMIN IS -- and Tg is one symbol. At PYUSD only the second delay exists, with no delay at all on the admin's actions, and Tg would be wrong there for exactly that reason (see the PYUSD record). Tg cannot distinguish 'the key acts slowly' from 'the key acts instantly but changes hands slowly', and those are opposite guarantees.

functionalObligations.text: USDG is deployed on Ethereum as an ERC-20, Solana as an SPL Token-2022, and Ink, X Layer and Robinhood Chain as ERC-20s, on distributed ledgers the white paper confirms the issuer does not operate.
functionalObligations.note: Xf and Xm are NOT CARRIED, deliberately. No primary statement of how USDG supply moves between these deployments could be found; the white paper describes per-chain issuance and describes no bridge. The mechanism is UNKNOWN and must not be assumed to be USD1's CCIP or anything else. This is a case where the honest record is an absence of evidence rather than evidence of absence, and the construction reflects that by carrying nothing.

functionalObligations.text: Ethereum supply is 500,509,895.398634 USDG at 6 decimals on 2026-08-04, a fraction of all-chain supply.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, as at USDT F12: no element names a fixed-unit balance. RANKING BASIS WARNING: Ethereum-only is US$500.5M against the corpus's US$3.42B all-chain DefiLlama figure at the same date -- a factor of roughly seven. Any later lane reading a single chain for this member will be badly wrong, and nothing in the model records which chain a supply figure came from.

functionalObligations.text: The contracts are published under MIT licence and audited: github.com/paxosglobal/usdg-contract and github.com/paxosglobal/paxos-token-contracts carry an audits directory holding Halborn on PaxosTokenV2 and Zellic on USDG Rewards and PAXG V2, with the USDG README naming Zellic and Trail of Bits.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. At is 'reserve / NAV / financial attestation'; a security audit is an attestation ABOUT CODE by a named firm with a stated scope, and it has no symbol. The category therefore has two independent assurance regimes -- one over the reserve, one over the contracts -- and the vocabulary names only the one that does not cover the code it is decomposing. Neither repository surfaced a release tag, so the citable artefact is the deployed verified source rather than a commit.

paper.title: Global Dollar USDG
paper.label: cat:fiat:usdg
paper.blurb: The only issuer of the five that runs a timelock, and the only one whose reward distribution happens on-chain rather than as an off-chain arrangement. Both facts are absent from the corpus record.
paper.witnessReason: The witness adds the timelock, the on-chain reward ledger with its share accounting and epoch gate, and the guardian --- elements the corpus assigned to nobody in this category, one of them established by reading the live facet table rather than the documentation.
paper.residueNote: And here the category's sharpest fact appears, which is a fact about a \emph{party}. A single externally-owned account is the freeze key for this issuer and for one other, and is simultaneously the sole proposer, executor and canceller of the timelock --- which does not cover the freeze. The vocabulary records that a timelock is present and that a freeze is present. It cannot record that they are the same key, that the key is one account rather than a quorum, or that the delay does not apply to the power that matters. This is the party sort, exhibited rather than conjectured.
